text: We need the ocean to live! It regulates the temperature of the Earth and contains phytoplankton, which are tiny little plants that produce the oxygen we need to breathe.

atoms.b: There are thousands of phytoplankton in one single drop of ((tap_water ++seawater))! They can even turn the water green when there is an extremely high quantity.
Sometimes, there are so many in one area that you can even see them from ((upstairs ++space))!
Phytoplankton take in carbon dioxide that has dissolved in the ocean. They then turn it into ((++oxygen carbon_dioxide)) through a process called photosynthesis.
Due to the vast amount of ((++phytoplankton photoseaweed)) in the ocean, they release around half of our total oxygen supply.

instruction.text: What else do you think phytoplankton helps to regulate?

feedback.finish: If there is too much carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, the Earth can get too hot. As phytoplankton consumes carbon dioxide, it helps to keep the Earth’s temperature right.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

hint.text: The orange line on the map shows the movement of warm water, and the purple shows the movement of cold water.

atoms.text: The ocean also absorbs heat from the Sun and makes the Earth warm enough for us to live on. This heat travels around the globe via continuous movements of water called currents. These currents are caused by wind and the Earth’s rotation and affect the climate of different places.

The Gulf Stream is the current that passes by the UK. It transports warm water from tropical areas to Northern Europe. This water heats up the air above it, which then blows over the UK, stopping it from becoming too cold in winter.
